summary: Thin Friday: 20 of 35 games researched (NHL, NFL, KHL, DEL, a Dota 2 and a CS2 series, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, La Liga, Premier League, Eredivisie, Belgian and Turkish football). Two kept at medium: Lokomotiv to win at Lada (KHL; Fonbet and Winline agree with Polymarket within 1-2 points; goalies unconfirmed, and Lada won both meetings this season 1-0) and the Devils to beat the Flames (NHL; DraftKings and Covers agree; Devils rested and healthy, goalies unconfirmed). Excluded: Rizespor v Kasımpaşa (coach status and team news could not be verified). Rated low, mostly for unconfirmed goalies or team news, or a 60-70% favourite with no second price: Flyers, Vegas, Broncos (Steelers released Rodgers; Rudolph starts), Bremen, Brest-Paris FC, Levante, Forest-Chelsea, Groningen (four straight losses), Red Bull München (number-one goalie out), Eisbären Berlin, Ingolstadt, Bremerhaven, SKA, Severstal, OH Leuven, PARIVISION v Liquid and M80 v 100 Thieves. The remaining games are coin flips or under 60%, which the pick cannot use. The slip is two legs at about 1.70, just under the usual range: about 53% to land, still negative expected value.

checks.team_news: DailyFaceoff (updated 26 Nov): Devils IR is Casey, Mantha, Kovacevic only; Jack and Luke Hughes, Hischier, Bratt, Meier and Hamilton are all in the lineup. Flames IR is Bahl and Huberdeau, Pospisil is out and Frost is day-to-day. No major Devils absence found; Flames are thin up front.
checks.lineups: Goalies unconfirmed as of this morning. DailyFaceoff's starting-goalies page shows Hellebuyck (9-1-0, 2.62 GAA, .899) for the Devils and Wolf (6-6-2, 3.42 GAA, .878) for Calgary, both marked unconfirmed. The team pages list Wolf ahead of Cooley and Hellebuyck ahead of Jake Allen. Devils lines: Meier-J.Hughes-Brown, Gritsyuk-Hischier-Bratt. Flames lines: Sharangovich-Backlund-Coronato, Farabee-Strome-Klapka. Only DailyFaceoff read; no beat-reporter confirmation or morning-skate report found.
checks.rotation: No back-to-back for either side. NJ played 25 Nov at Columbus (3-2 SO win) with no game on 26 Nov. Calgary played 25 Nov at Pittsburgh (6-3 win) with no game on 26 Nov. Calgary is on a road trip (this game, then at the Rangers on 28 Nov, then at Detroit on 1 Dec), so Wolf could be rested for a back-to-back, but the starter here is likely him. NJ's next game is home vs Winnipeg on 28 Nov, which makes a Devils backup goalie today a small risk.
checks.motivation: Standings 26 Nov: NJ 17-8-0, 34 pts, .680, 3rd in the East and 2nd in the Metropolitan. CGY 11-13-2, 24 pts, .462, 11th in the West and 4th in the Pacific. Early-season regular game for both, no rivalry. Coach: searches found no coaching change at either club in the last 7 days, but I could not positively confirm both coaches by name.
checks.form: NJ is 7-3-0 in its last 10 and 10-3-0 at home. Recent games: L 2-4 at WPG, W 5-2 WSH, W 7-4 at WSH, L 2-3 MTL, L 6-9 at STL, W 3-2 CBJ, W 3-2 SO at CBJ. Season GF/GA is 94/77, but the defence is leaky lately. CGY is 4-5-1 in its last 10 and 5-7-1 on the road, with GF/GA 67/89. Recent games: L 1-6 at ANA, W 5-2 at SJ, L 1-4 MIN, L 3-4 OT CHI, L 1-2 at OTT, W 6-3 at PIT.
checks.h2h: No 2026-27 meeting before today. Last season's meetings were not read in detail; the NHL.com previews in search results include a 12 March 2026 Devils-Flames game, with Calgary 25-32-7 and NJ 32-30-2 at that point. Overtime and shootout are a coin flip. NJ's last game went to a shootout, and Calgary's 21 Nov game went to overtime.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (read by the main task): Devils -285 (opened -265), Flames +230 (opened +215), about 71% for the Devils de-vigged. The line has moved slightly toward the Devils. Covers consensus is Flames +219 and Devils -250 (about 70% de-vigged). Covers also lists Novig 72%, ProphetX 72%, OG and Crypto.com 73% for the Devils. Polymarket is 70.5%, with a 24h move from 71.0% to 70.5% (relative -0.7%, under 3%). Independent prices agree with Polymarket within about 2 points.
checks.models: No MoneyPuck or Natural Stat Trick xG figures were fetched. Bookmaker-free proxies only: points percentage .680 vs .462, goal difference +17 vs -22, last-10 points 14 vs 9. All favour NJ clearly, consistent with a roughly 68-70% win chance including OT and SO.
checks.venue_weather: Prudential Center, Newark, a normal NJ home game at 1 PM ET (18:00 UTC), so Devils are really at home and the candidate file's 'home' (Flames) is the real away team. Neutral venue ruled out. Calgary is in the middle of a long road trip; the Devils are 10-3-0 at home. Indoor arena, so no weather factor.

games.reason: Market 70.5%, DraftKings about 71% and Covers consensus about 70-73% all agree, and the Devils are rested, healthy and clearly better on points percentage, goal difference and home record. I shaded the Devils slightly to 69% because both starters are unconfirmed, the Devils' defence has been leaky (9 goals against at STL), and an OT or SO decision is a coin flip. Within 5 points of p_market.
games.main_risk: Wolf standing on his head, or a backup in net for the Devils (Jake Allen instead of Hellebuyck, with a home game against Winnipeg the next night), with the game going to overtime or a shootout where a 70% favourite is only about 50-50.

checks.team_news: Steelers released QB Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday 25 Nov, so Mason Rudolph starts. Per sportsinteraction.com, Pittsburgh LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) and LB Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) are questionable. WR Ben Skowronek, G Mason McCormick and DT Sebastian Joseph-Day are out. Denver: RB RJ Harvey and DL Eyioma Uwazurike are out; S Brandon Jones (hamstring) and CB Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) are questionable. Bo Nix is the Broncos QB. I did not see a full final official report with Friday designations for Pat Surtain II, Zach Allen, Waddle or Mims, so Denver's secondary and defensive-line status is unconfirmed.
checks.lineups: Rudolph (backup, 19 career starts, one practice with the first team) starts for Pittsburgh. Nix starts for Denver. The sources I read agree on both QBs. I found no confirmed full starting lineup; the offensive-line and linebacker starters for both sides depend on the questionable tags above.
checks.rotation: Both teams played Sunday 22 Nov (Denver beat Las Vegas 38-24; Pittsburgh lost 19-16 to Philadelphia). Neither played on Thanksgiving, so both are on a short week, six days of rest. Denver travels to Pittsburgh, a minor factor. No rotation issue is reported.
checks.motivation: Denver is 8-2, on a six-game win streak, and in the AFC playoff and seeding race (3-2 on the road, 4-1 in the AFC). Pittsburgh is 6-4, tied with Cleveland for second in the AFC North, and is coming off two straight losses. Both teams still have something to play for. This is not a divisional game and not a fierce rivalry. I found no coaching changes. The Rodgers release is a QB change, not a coaching change.
checks.form: Denver: 8-2, six straight wins and covers, 38-24 over the Raiders in Week 11, and 17 straight one-score regular-season wins per sportsinteraction.com (a streak that tends to regress). 3-2 away. Pittsburgh: 6-4, lost 38-18 to Cincinnati and 19-16 to Philadelphia, 4-0 at home. Rodgers was sacked five times against the Eagles.
checks.h2h: I found no h2h data in the pages I read, so this is unverified. Style matchup: Denver has a top pass rush (No. 1 PFF pass-rush grade, sixth in pressure rate) against a backup QB behind an offensive line missing McCormick. That favours Denver, but a defence-heavy game with a 36.5-37.5 total tends to stay close. Not a rivalry.
checks.odds: DraftKings on ESPN (read by the main task): opening Steelers -102 / Broncos -118, current Steelers +204 / Broncos -247, de-vigged to Denver 68.4%. News that explains the move: the Rodgers release on Wednesday and the switch to Rudolph. The spread moved from Denver -1.5/-2.5 to -3.5/-4.5, and the total is 36.5-37.5. A second price from cbssports.com shows Broncos -228 / Steelers +190, de-vigged to about 66.8% Denver. Polymarket (68.5%), DraftKings (68.4%) and the CBS price (66.8%) agree within about 2 points. Public betting is heavily on Denver (about 88% of tickets), so the price may carry a public premium.
checks.models: I found no FPI, Elo or point-differential figures. covers.com notes Denver ranks fifth in EPA per play over the last five weeks, 11th in offensive DVOA and eighth in defensive DVOA. SportsLine's model projects a 40-point total and Denver to cover, per cbssports.com. The spread of -4.5 implies roughly 65-68%, consistent with the market.
checks.venue_weather: Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh, outdoors, kickoff 3 p.m. ET. Forecasts differ. covers.com has southwest wind about 17 mph with gusts near 28 mph, about 42F, and a 65% chance of rain at kickoff. sportsinteraction.com has about 41F, a 35% chance of precipitation, and a wet field after heavy rain on Thursday. Wind and rain mean lower scoring and more variance, which helps the underdog. Not extreme enough to exclude, and not a neutral venue. The candidate file's 'home' (Broncos) is the real away team.

games.reason: The market (Polymarket 68.5%, DraftKings de-vig 68.4%, CBS de-vig about 66.8%) agrees, and the late move toward Denver is explained by Pittsburgh releasing Rodgers on Wednesday, which leaves Rudolph with one practice. I shaded Denver down to 65.5%, because the big move and the 88% public ticket share may overstate Denver's edge, Denver's 17 straight one-score wins is unlikely to continue, and the wind and rain add variance in a low-total game. Pittsburgh is 4-0 at home. Confidence is low, because favourites at 60-70% and NFL results have underperformed in our record, Denver's injury designations were not fully confirmed, and I found no independent model win probability.
games.main_risk: A low-scoring game in wind and rain where turnovers and a late score decide it. Rudolph plays a clean, conservative game, Pittsburgh's defence and the home crowd keep it within one score, and Denver's luck in close games runs out.

Flyers: only Nikita Grebenkin (back) listed out. Search snippets say Ristolainen is not on the list. No beat-reporter or team X confirmation found.

Nothing found for 26 Nov (no NHL games found). Canucks' previous game and travel (Eastern trip) not verified; I could not confirm whether they played on 25 Nov.
checks.motivation: Canucks 6-20-1, last in the NHL (and 6-game losing streak earlier this month); Flyers 9-12-6, also under .500 so not a high-stakes game for either. Coaches: Philadelphia has Rick Tocchet; Vancouver has Manny Malhotra (first season, per THN 10 Nov); no coaching change in the last 7 days found for either team, though I did not check team sites directly. Tocchet is the former Canucks coach, a mild storyline, not a fierce rivalry.
checks.form: Flyers 9-12-6 and just lost 3-7 at home vs Washington on 25 Nov; the Canucks are 6-20-1 with a long skid and a weak roster missing Pettersson and Demko. Last-10 goals for/against and home/away splits were not retrieved.
checks.h2h: Flyers beat the Canucks 3-1 on 9 Nov 2026 in Vancouver (Merilainen in net for Vancouver, Canucks' skid reached six). Last season's meetings include a 5-2 Flyers win in Philadelphia on 22 Dec 2025. Games ending level in regulation not assessed.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (read by the main task): Flyers -245 (opened -230), Canucks +200 (opened +190), de-vigged about 68.1% Flyers; total 6.5. Bleacher Nation (snippet) shows Flyers -244, which is the same price family, not independent. Polymarket 68.5% is in line. Slight drift toward the favourite, no adverse move. No true second independent book found.
checks.models: No MoneyPuck, Natural Stat Trick or Opta page was retrieved, so no independent model view. Points percentage alone (Flyers about .389 vs Canucks about .241) supports the favourite but 9-12-6 is a mediocre team.
checks.venue_weather: Real home team is the Flyers (Xfinity Mobile Arena, Philadelphia, standard NHL venue, 3 PM ET Black Friday matinee, indoors). Candidate file maps 'home' = Canucks only because Polymarket names them first. Not a neutral venue. Canucks travel from the West coast for an early-afternoon start (possible fatigue for them).

games.reason: Market and DraftKings agree at about 68%, and the Canucks (6-20-1, without Pettersson and Demko) look weak, so the Flyers deserve to be the favourite. I shade the Flyers from 0.685 to 0.67 because neither goalie is confirmed, Vladar may start after Woll played on 25 Nov, the Flyers are themselves 9-12-6 and on the first night of a back-to-back, and no independent price or model was found. Favourites at 60-70% have underperformed in our record, so confidence is low.
games.main_risk: Backup goalie (Vladar) in net for the Flyers on the first night of a back-to-back, or a hot Merilainen/Lankinen, with the game decided in overtime or a shootout coin flip.

The line has drifted slightly toward Vegas, not against. The second price is a pick-site line, not an independent book page. Polymarket 65.5% (up from 64.5% in 24h) agrees with the books.

checks.venue_weather: SAP Center, San Jose. San Jose is the real home team and Vegas the visitor, while the candidate file lists Vegas as home. Puck drop is 1 PM PT / 21:00 UTC. Vegas is on a short trip, with the 3-game road trip ending. Indoor arena, so no weather issue. ESPN, iHeart and Vegas Hockey Knight agree on the fixture.

games.reason: The market and DraftKings agree at roughly 65-66% for Vegas, which fits Vegas's strong record against a weak, injured Sharks team. I shade Vegas down to 63% because the goalies are unconfirmed and sources conflict on Hill versus Hart. Vegas's injury picture is unverified. Favourites priced 60-70% have a weak record with us. Hockey overtime and shootout keep every game close to a coin flip. Confidence is low since several checks (goalie, injuries, schedule) are not confirmed.
games.main_risk: A backup or off-form goalie for Vegas, or a hot Askarov, makes it a low-scoring game that goes to overtime or a shootout, where Vegas's edge is small.

A second price was not found: searches for OddsPortal, HLTV betting and Bo3.gg odds returned nothing for this match, and HLTV and Liquipedia returned 403. The favourite lengthened from 61.5% to 64.5% in 24h (+4.9% relative) with no news found to explain it. The move is in the favourite's favour, but with no independent price I cannot confirm it.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free model was found. Wikipedia says Stage 1 is seeded by Valve Regional Standings, but gives no VRS or HLTV rank for either team. Round difference favours 100 Thieves (+5 vs -7) in a very small sample.
checks.venue_weather: All Stage 1 matches are in Singapore (PGL Major Singapore 2026); LAN or online was not stated on the pages read, and the playoffs are at the Singapore Indoor Stadium. Format confirmed: Bo3 at a tier-1 Valve Major, Round 5 on 27 Nov.

games.reason: The event is the PGL Major Singapore 2026 Stage 1, Round 5. It is a Bo3 tier-1 Major, so it passes the format gate, and there are no roster or stand-in issues. The market gives 100 Thieves 64.5%. I trimmed that to 62.5% because both sides are 2-2 with decider pressure, M80 has a stable roster that knows this stage, and CS2 favourites priced 60-70% have a weak record. I found no independent price to back the +4.9% move, and the round-difference gap is small.
games.main_risk: M80 win a high-variance Bo3 decider. A single map upset or a poor veto by 100 Thieves is enough. 100 Thieves lost 6-13 and 5-13 maps in their last two series and are prone to heavy map losses.

games.reason: I started from the market. Polymarket (57.7 / 21.7 / 20.6) and the de-vigged DraftKings price (55.8 / 22.1 / 22.1) agree within 2 points, and SoccerVital's de-vigged 1.80 / 4.40 / 4.30 is slightly lower on Bremen. I trimmed Bremen to 56% and set Gladbach at 22% to match the DraftKings away drift (3.8 to 4.2) and Gladbach's many late goals. Bremen are clearly stronger on table and form (6th against 18th, W4 D1 at home, 4-0 last time out, Füllkrug on 10 goals). Confidence is low because no press conference or reliable injury report was found and the sources disagree on who is out for both sides.
games.main_risk: A draw or late Gladbach equaliser: Gladbach have conceded 9 goals in the last 15 minutes of games, their counter-attacks are dangerous, the last meeting ended 1-1 with a stoppage-time Bremen equaliser, and the new coach Blessin may be reorganising a side with 8 losses.
